content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early cycles, especially when sentiment is bullish.", "Sentiment spikes near the end of history often trigger a sharp price surge not captured in initial forecasts.", "Models show mean-reversion bias in later periods, underestimating sustained upward momentum.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment aligns with historical price trends, particularly in mid-to-late cycles.", "Early forecast lags are common, with models missing the first 3–5 days of true price movement.", "High sentiment volatility correlates with forecast overshoots, especially in the first 10 days of the forecast window.", "Models underperform when sentiment turns negative, failing to anticipate sharp downward corrections.", "Forecast calibration should adjust for sentiment-driven momentum shifts, especially after 15-day mark in the forecast horizon."]}
